complexity.notes: Unit-cost reporting makes this O(n), but the real work is digit-level: each 10**i and the final big-integer multiply make the true bit-level cost superlinear, which is why this feels slower than it looks. The intended approach avoids ever materializing the big integers by ||accumulating single-digit products into a positions array indexed by i+j||, which keeps all arithmetic on small digits. Also note that building the integer by hand with ord() rather than int() technically respects the no-built-in-conversion rule, though it sidesteps its spirit.
complexity.summary: Reconstructs each integer by summing digit values times powers of 10, multiplies the two big integers, and converts the result back with str.
